source.title: $C$-$\Delta\Theta$: Circuit-Restricted Weight Arithmetic for Selective Refusal
source.authors: Aditya Kasliwal; Pratinav Seth; Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates an activation-steering baseline that adds a contrastive residual-stream direction and reports refusal behavior. Its direction construction and intervention differ from the claimed difference-in-means direction ablated across all layers and positions.
record.gate_note: Rows below cover only the paper's Activation Steering (AS) baseline, which adds a residual-stream direction and reports harmless- and harmful-prompt refusal rates. C-∆Θ and weight-steering results are not rows for these versions: they edit weights rather than the claimed residual-stream direction. The paper's per-cell steering strengths and its direction-selection hyperparameters are not outcomes.
record.test_reason: The only direction intervention is the Activation Steering (AS) baseline, used as a comparator for the paper's own weight-editing method (C-∆Θ). Its vector is not the claimed harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction. Per App. G.2 it is built from 100 harmless Alpaca prompts with refusal-template versus compliance-template suffixes. App. D.1 describes the same vector as the first PCA component, a second description that conflicts with G.2. Layers and scales were tuned to reach ≥90% harmful refusal (Table 7). AS is reported only as a competing method's performance. There is no ablation, no mediation test, and no capability check for AS. None of the rows measures the direction V1 names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that circuit-restricted weight arithmetic (C-∆Θ) yields selective refusal checkpoints that Pareto-dominate AS, CAST and unmasked weight steering at matched harmful refusal, with small utility loss. They name EAP-IG site selection as the load-bearing step. They also claim refusal is carried by a shared sparse MLP subnetwork, bimodal across depth. They make no claim about a single residual direction.
record.recipe_differences: The evaluated AS baseline derives a PCA vector from contrastive activations and injects it at selected layers. It does not use the claimed direct harmful-minus-harmless mean direction or test projection-out across every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: AS layer ranges vary by model; the reported harmless-refusal rates vary substantially by model (22.2%-68.0%) and harmful category. The paper says AS parameters for Llama-3.1 follow the cited protocol and others are found by heuristic search.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a refusal- vs compliance-template steering vector (built on harmless Alpaca prompts) at tuned layers raises harmful refusal to 39.4–92.4%. It also raises harmless refusal to 22.2–68.0% across six instruct models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding a refusal-completion contrastive activation vector induces refusal on both harmful and harmless prompts, with poor selectivity.

fits_no_version.finding: An EAP-IG refusal circuit over MLP output channels on Llama-3.1-8B is bimodal: dense at early layers (1–6) and the final layer, sparse mid-network. Per-category masks overlap (mean Jaccard 0.571).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-relevant MLP-output computation is a shared sparse subnetwork concentrated at early and final layers.

record.code_released: The paper says it will publicly release the training code and evaluation harness; no URL is stated.
record.problems: Evidence for V1 is limited to an activation-steering comparator, not an ablation or full causal mediation test. The direction intervention's capability retention is not reported; capability measurements are for C-∆Θ. The paper reports a single random seed and gives no uncertainty estimates for the refusal-rate results. AS produces substantial harmless-prompt refusal (22.2%-68.0%) across the reported settings.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant AS outcome rows were left out. Other methods' refusal and utility results were excluded because they do not apply, remove, add, or measure the claimed residual-stream direction.

untested.parts: No harmful-minus-harmless direction, no ablation, no mediation test, and no capability retention for any direction intervention.
No abliteration or weight edit removing a residual direction. The ethics section only notes that −α∆θ could suppress refusal, and this is untested.
Not tested. The circuit and Jaccard analyses concern MLP channels, not direction geometry.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' and V1 'supports' label are rejected. AS is a baseline comparator and its direction is a different construct from the claimed direction. It is described as PCA in App. D.1 but as a mean difference in App. G.2, and is built from completion templates rather than harmful vs harmless instructions. Its strength was tuned to reach high harmful refusal. The harmless-refusal values are one model-wide number per model, repeated across categories. Single seed, no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The AS baseline tests adding a contrastive direction, but not ablating the direction, projecting it out of every layer and position, or testing whether that direction mediates refusal. Utility-retention results are for C-∆Θ checkpoints, not the AS direction intervention.
No released-model weight edit that removes the claimed direction or tests abliteration.
No test of attacks suppressing the claimed direction or training against its ablation.
The paper's circuit and category-overlap analyses do not test whether refusal is affine, conical, or carried by a dominant direction plus others.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer test across languages, model variants using a shared direction, or base-to-instruct transfer. AS vectors are evaluated per model.
No comparison of how refusal training choices determine whether one removable direction exists.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: AS adds a contrastive activation vector to the residual stream at specified layers.
rows.locator: Table 1; AS layer configuration in Appendix Table 7
rows.note: AS vector is extracted using PCA on contrastive refusal/compliance activation differences; the paper reports rates for both prompt types.
rows.check: Comparator row for a baseline method. The direction is refusal- vs compliance-template on harmless Alpaca prompts, not harmful-minus-harmless instructions. Layers and scale were tuned for high harmful refusal. The harmless rate (25.0) is one model-wide value repeated across categories.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: AS direction addition across the six instruction-tuned models and five reported harm categories
reader_labels.reason: AS raises harmless-prompt refusal above the base rate in every reported cell, consistent with direction addition inducing refusal; this does not establish ablation or mediation. Rows r01-r30.
